## Triage — stopping here, this is a decision, not a build

**In plain English.** Agents keep starting work without a triaged issue and without your sign-off, and keep picking wide-blast-radius approaches to narrow requests. A rule was added to `CLAUDE.md` to stop it, but a rule is just text an agent chooses to follow at the exact moment it's most tempted not to — and it has already failed more than once. The issue asks whether to make the gate *mechanical* instead of advisory. That's your call to make, and it's the one thing that has to be settled before anything gets built.

### Why triage isn't planning this one

Every option on the table changes **how agents are allowed to work on this repo** — including whether an agent may edit `CLAUDE.md`, and whether the rule #1 text and its renumbering (`1f980ae`) should stand, be reworked, or be reverted. Picking one of those in triage would be a fresh instance of the exact pattern the issue is about: an agent choosing a high-blast-radius approach to a request without surfacing the choice first. So this rests on your ruling.

Two observations that may help you choose, offered as input, not as a recommendation being acted on:

- **A and B are genuinely different failures, and A doesn't catch B.** The issue already notes this and it holds: a `PreToolUse` hook denying edits to `Assets/**` / `CoreTests/**` / `ProjectSettings/**` would not have blocked the `CLAUDE.md` renumbering, because that was a docs edit. Option A addresses "built without an issue"; option B addresses "picked a churny approach to work that *was* asked for." Whatever you pick, it's worth deciding them as two questions rather than one.
- **Option A has a bootstrapping wrinkle worth pricing in.** A hook that requires an approved issue number before touching `Assets/**` has to get that number from somewhere the triage flow writes (env var or a file). If that plumbing isn't in place, the hook either blocks all development or is trivially satisfied by any agent that can set the variable — in which case it's advisory again, just with more moving parts. Not an argument against A; it's the part that decides whether A is ~30 lines or considerably more.

Whichever way this goes, the verification bar is already stated well in the issue and doesn't need restating: an agent handed a bug report with no issue, and an agent told to make a small change to a shared file, both **demonstrably** stop and hand back.
